title: Fix stale PR148 source-retention blocker in generated ledger
head: 26ef95ac9394fd343848a2ad37d21b9e91e0ea13
body:
The generated PR148 ledger still said fourteen changed paths lacked source coverage, although Thiago Goulart's incorporated PR1572 receipt already authenticates all 114 paths. A ledger rebuild reproduced that obsolete blocker. This patch teaches `reconcile_pr_queue.py` to consume the retained RESULT/COVERAGE receipts and records their exact-head source-only coverage in the generated JSON and Markdown.

The original recovery and authenticated Git-tree proof remain credited to PR1572; Rohan Gupta retains PR148 construction credit. The remaining question now asks for the complete historical mathematical review of the eleven-file direct author delta. PR148 remains partially reviewed, open and draft. No review-completion flags, incorporation location or closure state are upgraded, and historical decisions stay unchanged.

The supplement applies to the pinned PR148 head `975c3cf5d4ee0c90d5a76500d431bfc59102bb72`. If a later head appears, the evidence stays historical and the current obligation is preserved. A later completed review is not reopened. Receipt coverage/head inconsistencies fail before changing the row, and repeated application is idempotent.

Validation on CPython 3.12.14:

```sh
python3.12 -I -O -B research/pr148-source-retention/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B scripts/test_pr148_ledger_retention.py
python3.12 -X utf8 -B scripts/reconcile_pr_queue.py
```

The unchanged PR1572 proof passed 114 paths = 96 main + 4 archive + 14 recovered, with eleven direct changes. Four regression groups pass, including seven inconsistent-receipt cases, changed-head preservation, no reopening of later review and idempotence. Two complete generator runs are identical. Comparison with base shows only PR148 changes among 1,685 rows; all 1,684 other rows and every disposition count are unchanged. A separate Codex agent reviewed the change and independently ran the four groups with CPython 3.12.7, finding no blocker.

The optional full `python3.12 -X utf8 -I -O -B scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py` does not pass: after the frontier799 checks it reaches an existing frontier890 pin mismatch for `research/single-intersection-spectrum-audit/RESULT.json`. That file is unchanged and byte-identical to base main (SHA256 `861ab5505282cfe13a7088a12217797f6da947a47e407d93d67843d1fa655f92`); the historical receipt expects `9cb2210e148b2cce3fe59cf529fbf99f3b663dc7673db2e3969246595692f580`. This unrelated historical reconciliation is not modified here. No selected cold replay or mathematical PR148 execution is claimed.

Selection: consolidation / overlap-receipt, seed `243bca9b614d2052089c3d493c354dce`, scope key `757723e3fd38f20fa774`. The required `scripts/research_baseline.py` first command passed. Canonical main was freshly fetched unchanged at `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority 4. Complete overlap covered 798 open PRs and 1,252 Discussion records at 15:55/15:59 UTC on 2026-10-15; a recent 100-PR screen at 16:12 UTC found no matching ledger fix. Live PR148 is still the same open draft head. Metadata searches do not cover every diff or establish novelty.

Open next questions: reconstruct the complete historical PR148 verification from its authenticated tree and audit its eleven-file direct delta; separately reconcile the old frontier890 result pin before claiming a global ledger-integrity pass. Source coverage alone settles neither question.

Credit Douglas Colkitt's ledger generator, Thiago Goulart / Tuafo's PR1572 source-retention proof, Rohan Gupta / gupt1156's PR148 construction and the existing review lineage. New generator reconciliation and regressions by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate-agent review. Apache-2.0; no independent human or formal-kernel review claimed.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
